Legal Standards.name: Agricultural Revenue (Private Sector)
Legal Standards.note: There are no legally established standards governing private-sector agricultural revenue; revenue outcomes are not directly regulated.

Legal Standards.name: Irrigation Water Supply (Agricultural Input)
Legal Standards.note: Legal standards apply to irrigation water supply as a regulated and essential input to agriculture, distinct from agricultural revenue itself.

Legal Standards.name: USDA Disaster Assistance and Risk Management Programs
Legal Standards.note: Publicly authorized and funded programs that are not legally mandated entitlements; participation is voluntary and accessed through application processes administered by USDA.

programs.name: Drought Assistance
programs.criteria: U.S. Drought Monitor ratings; loss thresholds often apply

programs.name: Price Loss Coverage (PLC)
programs.basis: Commodity price declines relative to statutory reference prices

programs.name: Emergency Relief Program (ERP)
programs.basis: Congressional authorization for disaster-related revenue losses

Legal Standards.name: Irrigation Water Rights Priority
Legal Standards.note: Irrigation rights are protected under constitutional and statutory water-rights frameworks, following the principle of priority in time, and are subordinate only to human health and safety needs.

key_elements.constraint: Human health and safety needs take precedence

Tier 1.note: Curtailments affect junior water rights holders when water is scarce. They are triggered by drought or water unavailability, not by agricultural revenue changes.

Tier 1.policy_name: State and federal economic policy responses
Tier 1.note: Revenue losses due to curtailments may activate economic support measures; changes in agricultural revenue track drought conditions but do not directly trigger curtailments.

Tier 2.policy_name: Water for irrigation / water rights enforcement
Tier 2.note: Curtailments follow constitutional water use priorities and rights, ensuring allocation aligns with seniority and scarcity conditions.
Direct producer grants, technical assistance, farm business management, financial planning, and marketing support are provided to farms affected by curtailed water deliveries.
Increased dependence on groundwater triggers reduced pumping or curtailment orders, fees, and potential land fallowing under local GSA authority.

Tier 3.note: Policies implemented in Tier 2 continue and are reinforced under more severe water scarcity conditions.

Tier 4.policy_name: Curtailment, groundwater, and local water source management
Tier 4.note: Unprecedented drought or catastrophic conditions result in full reliance on groundwater and local sources. Water supplies are heavily reduced and allocated only for basic human health, safety, and food security.
Emergency water planning measures are implemented to allocate scarce resources to critical human and food needs.
